We need propose a 3-step retrosynthesis for target: Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2)cc1.

We have guidance: steps are (forward) 1) amide formation (carboxylic acid + amine). 2) Doebner modification (aldehyde + malonic acid -> α,β-unsaturated acid). 3) sulfonamide formation (amine + sulfonyl chloride). So retrosynthetic steps reverse: target -> break amide to give acid and aniline; break α,β-unsaturated acid to aldehyde + malonic acid? Actually Doebner modification forward: aldehyde + malonic acid -> α,β-unsaturated acid. So reverse: unsaturated acid -> aldehyde + malonic acid. Then sulfonamide formation forward: amine + sulfonyl chloride -> sulfonamide. Reverse: sulfonamide -> amine + sulfonyl chloride.

Thus we need three disconnections:

Target contains sulfonamide linking an aniline (para-methyl phenyl) to sulfonyl phenyl with unsaturated amide side chain. So step 3 (reverse) break sulfonamide: give sulfonyl chloride (aryl sulfonyl chloride) and aniline (the first phenyl with methyl). The sulfonyl chloride is attached to second phenyl ring (the one bearing the unsaturated amide). So product after step 3: aniline (para-methyl aniline) and aryl sulfonyl chloride (with the unsaturated amide side chain attached). Step 2 reverse: the unsaturated amide side chain is an α,β-unsaturated carboxylic acid attached to the aryl sulfonyl chloride via the aromatic ring. Actually the unsaturated amide is C(=O)N-aryl (anilide) attached to the double bond. The unsaturated acid is the part before amide formation: α,β-unsaturated carboxylic acid attached to aromatic ring. So reverse amide formation: break amide to give carboxylic acid (α,β-unsaturated) and aniline (the second phenyl with amine). So after step 2 we have aryl sulfonyl chloride with α,β-unsaturated acid attached, and aniline (c3ccccc3N). Step 1 reverse Doebner: unsaturated acid -> aldehyde (aryl aldehyde) + malonic acid. The aldehyde is attached to the aromatic ring (the same phenyl). So final precursors: aryl sulfonyl chloride (with aldehyde substituent) and malonic acid, plus the first aniline (para-methyl aniline). Wait we also need the amine for amide formation (the aniline that becomes amide). That's the second phenyl (c3ccccc3N). So final set: 1) para-methyl aniline (for sulfonamide formation). 2) aryl sulfonyl chloride bearing aldehyde (for Doebner then amide). 3) malonic acid (for Doebner). Actually the sulfonyl chloride is attached to the phenyl that also bears the aldehyde. So we need a phenyl sulfonyl chloride with aldehyde substituent at para position relative? In target, the sulfonyl phenyl is attached to sulfonamide nitrogen, and also has the unsaturated chain at para position? Let's examine SMILES: Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2)cc1

First phenyl: Cc1ccc(... )cc1 is para-methyl phenyl with NSO2 attached at para? Actually the NSO2 attaches at position 4 relative to methyl. So sulfonamide nitrogen attached to sulfonyl phenyl (c2ccc(... )cc2). That phenyl has the unsaturated amide side chain at para position relative to sulfonyl? The SMILES shows c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2 attached to sulfonyl S. So the unsaturated amide side chain is para to the sulfonyl attachment.

Thus the aryl sulfonyl chloride precursor would be the same phenyl with a sulfonyl chloride (SO2Cl) attached to nitrogen? Actually sulfonyl chloride is attached to the phenyl as SO2Cl group (aryl sulfonyl chloride). In target, the sulfonyl group is attached to nitrogen (sulfonamide). So the precursor would be aryl sulfonyl chloride (Ar-SO2Cl) where Ar is the phenyl bearing the unsaturated side chain (as aldehyde after reverse Doebner). So we need to generate that.

Thus propose route:

Step 1 (retro): Disconnection of sulfonamide: target -> para-methyl aniline (C c1ccc(N)cc1) and aryl sulfonyl chloride precursor: ClS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(CHO)cc2 (where CHO is aldehyde). Actually after step 2 we will have aldehyde, not unsaturated acid. So sulfonyl chloride with aldehyde.

Step 2 (retro): Disconnection of amide: aryl sulfonyl chloride with aldehyde attached to phenyl and amide side chain becomes: aryl sulfonyl chloride with α,β-unsaturated carboxylic acid attached (instead of amide). So we get aryl sulfonyl chloride with unsaturated acid (Ar-SO2Cl with /C=C/CO2H). The amine (aniline) is released.

Step 3 (retro): Disconnection of unsaturated acid via Doebner: unsaturated acid -> aldehyde (Ar-CHO) + malonic acid.

Thus final precursors: para-methyl aniline, aryl sulfonyl chloride (Ar-SO2Cl) where Ar is phenyl with aldehyde (or maybe with aldehyde after step 3). Actually after step 3 we have aldehyde, which then after step 2 amide formation uses aniline (c3ccccc3N) to give amide. So the aldehyde is on the same phenyl as sulfonyl chloride. So final set: para-methyl aniline, aryl sulfonyl chloride (with aldehyde), malonic acid.

Now we need to produce JSON route with three reaction nodes.

We need template IDs for each reaction. We can search for templates matching sulfonamide formation (amine + sulfonyl chloride). Let's search.
